title: Bihar Arrests Cross 450 as Student Protest Deal Unravels Over FIR Withdrawals
excerpt: Despite the Centre's agreement to drop cases against NEET protesters, Bihar police have detained over 450 people, prompting the Cockroach Janta Party to threaten fresh agitation and the Supreme Court to take up the matter.
body:
• Bihar police have arrested over 450 people linked to student protests despite the Centre's agreement to withdraw all FIRs against demonstrators.
  • The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has threatened to resume its agitation, alleging a "complete breach" of the deal struck after its 36-day protest at Jantar Mantar.
  • A Bihar constable has been suspended after video showed him firing an AK-47 at protesters in Siwan; the Supreme Court will hear a challenge to police action on Tuesday.
  • Opposition leaders, including Tejashwi Yadav and Rahul Gandhi, have issued ultimatums and demanded the immediate release of all detained students.

Two days after the Centre struck a deal with student protesters to end five weeks of nationwide agitation, the agreement is already fraying. Bihar police have arrested more than 450 people in connection with protests across the state, according to officials, even as the Cockroach Janta Party warns it will return to the streets if detainees are not freed and FIRs withdrawn.

The Deal That Ended the Protests

The CJP called off its 36-day sit-in at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Saturday after the central government accepted its key demands. Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned over leaked question papers for the NEET medical entrance exam, which more than two million students had taken in May. Health Minister J.P. Nadda, speaking alongside CJP representatives after a third round of negotiations, confirmed the government would withdraw police cases against peaceful protesters, compensate families of students who died by suicide following the paper leak, and consider a five-point charter on examination reforms.

https://x.com/SauravDassss/status/2081781841326190826

"All the demands raised by our team have been accepted, therefore we request protesters to withdraw and peacefully go home."

— Ashutosh Ranka, CJP Spokesperson

"The bottom line is we have won, your struggle, hard work, and patience have paid off," Ranka told cheering crowds at Jantar Mantar before urging them to disperse.

Bihar's Crackdown Continues

On the ground in Bihar, the picture looks different. Authorities say around 450 people have been arrested under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita in connection with violence during the Bihar Bandh on July 22 and subsequent protests on July 25. Some 200 detainees were produced before a magistrate at the Chhajjubagh judicial residence on Sunday night, with family members waiting outside. Police have released photographs of individuals identified as alleged troublemakers in several districts, including Patna.

Among those arrested are former Bihar minister Tej Pratap Yadav and CPI(ML) MLA Sandeep Saurav. Tej Pratap has been remanded to 14-day judicial custody and lodged in Beur Central Jail; his bail application is pending.

The most explosive incident came from Siwan, where widely circulated video showed a constable in riot gear running toward protesters and firing an AK-47-style rifle. Deputy Inspector General Nilesh Kumar confirmed the incident to Reuters, saying the constable belonged to an intelligence unit that "deals with dreaded, hard-core criminals" and had been issued the assault rifle.

"The AK-47 was used by the constable wrongly. It cannot be justified in any way. He used it wrongly, because they were students. There was no need of doing so."

— Nilesh Kumar, Deputy Inspector General of Police, Bihar

The constable has been suspended pending an inquiry. Senior police officials said no one was wounded by the gunfire, though reports from other protest sites indicate injuries from police action.

Opposition and Courts Step In

Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Assembly, issued a 24-hour ultimatum to Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary's NDA government on Sunday. "When it was decided yesterday that the cases would be withdrawn, how is this being handled separately in Bihar?" he asked reporters in Patna. He warned the RJD would launch a larger statewide movement if detainees were not released.

Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, alleged on social media that security forces had used AK-47 rifles against students and that hundreds had been arrested. "Where is your promise that no FIRs would be filed against students?" he directed at Prime Minister Modi.

Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge raised the issue in Parliament on Monday, calling it "one of the gravest assaults on democracy in our history." Government ministers did not respond before both houses were adjourned amid uproar.

RJD Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha has filed a Public Interest Litigation in the Supreme Court challenging the legality of the police response, including the use of firearms. The matter has been listed before the Chief Justice's bench, with a hearing expected on Tuesday.

What's Next

The CJP's threat to resume protests hangs over the government. Spokesperson Ranka wrote on X that the group was "observing a complete breach of the agreement" and demanded that all FIRs be withdrawn immediately, all students released, and no future cases filed "by Delhi Police, central investigative agencies, or police in BJP-allied states." CPI(ML) has announced a statewide Protest Day on July 30.

The Supreme Court hearing on Tuesday could prove pivotal. A ruling on the legality of police action — particularly the use of assault weapons against unarmed protesters — would set precedent for how authorities handle the ongoing unrest. Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, in a rare public comment by a sitting judge, said on Saturday: "It will not be an exaggeration to say that public space for expressing divergent opinion is shrinking in India."

For now, Bihar remains the epicentre of a crisis that has already cost one minister his job. Whether the state's crackdown undermines the fragile deal struck in Delhi — or forces a new round of confrontation — depends largely on what happens in the next 48 hours.
